_llm_instructions: Fill out the 'project_title' and 'date_prepared' properties, and the 'value' property of each field below, based on the available project context. Refer to parameters.md for the shared project variables. Name the model version, the group affected, and the threshold that triggers action, rather than recording a category; a governance plan that says 'encrypted', 'minimised' and 'monitored' describes an intention and not a system, and the difference only becomes visible when something goes wrong and no one can say what was in force.
form_name: AI MODEL CARD AND FACT SHEET

f01_Model_Name_and_Version.label: Model Name and Version
f01_Model_Name_and_Version.guidance: The model at a specific version, with the date that version was produced. A card that names a model rather than a version describes whichever build happens to be deployed when it is read, and the answer is rarely the one that was assessed.

f02_Developer_and_Provenance.label: Developer and Provenance
f02_Developer_and_Provenance.guidance: Who built it, whether it was trained in-house, fine-tuned, or acquired, and from what base model. Provenance determines which of the sections that follow can be answered at all, and it is usually the section that is missing when a question is asked.

f03_Architecture_and_Configuration.label: Architecture and Configuration
f03_Architecture_and_Configuration.guidance: The architecture family, the parameter count, and the settings that affect behaviour. The settings are the part that matters, because the same architecture with different decoding parameters is a different system.

f04_Training_Method_and_Compute.label: Training Method and Compute
f04_Training_Method_and_Compute.guidance: How it was trained, over what period, and at what cost. Compute is recorded because it bounds reproducibility: a result that needed a compute allocation nobody can obtain again is not a result that can be re-derived.

f05_Licence_and_Usage_Terms.label: Licence and Usage Terms
f05_Licence_and_Usage_Terms.guidance: The licence, who may use it, and under what restrictions. A model used outside its licence is a legal exposure that no technical section of this card addresses.

f06_Related_Artefacts.label: Related Artefacts
f06_Related_Artefacts.guidance: The model, the code, the weights and the data, each with where it lives. A card that lists no locations is a description, and a description cannot be checked against anything.

f07_Primary_Use.label: Primary Use
f07_Primary_Use.guidance: The task the model is for, stated as an input and an output. An input and an output can be tested; a purpose cannot.

f08_Secondary_Use.label: Secondary Use
f08_Secondary_Use.guidance: What else it may legitimately be used for, if anything. Recorded separately because a use that is merely tolerated and one that is endorsed need different controls, and a card that lists only the endorsed one hides the tolerated ones.

f09_Out_of_Scope_Use.label: Out-of-Scope Use
f09_Out_of_Scope_Use.guidance: The uses it must not be used for, with the reason for each. This section is the one that makes the card usable by someone deciding whether to deploy it, and a card without it can only say what the model is for.

f10_User_and_Audience.label: User and Audience
f10_User_and_Audience.guidance: Who operates it, and who is subject to its output. The two are routinely treated as one, and the conflation is how a system that scores applicants comes to be described as a tool that helps recruiters write better.

f11_Operating_Conditions.label: Operating Conditions
f11_Operating_Conditions.guidance: The inputs it expects, the conditions it was tested under, and the conditions under which it should not be used. These are the boundaries of the evaluation in section 4, and a metric read outside them is not a weaker claim, it is a wrong one.

f12_Human_Oversight_Requirement.label: Human Oversight Requirement
f12_Human_Oversight_Requirement.guidance: Where a person must review an output before it is acted on. Oversight specified as a general principle rather than as points in a workflow does not survive contact with a deadline.

f13_Datasets.label: Datasets
f13_Datasets.guidance: Each dataset by name, with its owner and the date it was collected. A dataset named only by type cannot be checked for permission, and permission is what blocks first.

f14_Provenance_and_Collection_Method.label: Provenance and Collection Method
f14_Provenance_and_Collection_Method.guidance: Where each dataset came from and how it was gathered. Collected data carries the practices of the period and place it came from, whether or not those were examined.

f15_Demographic_and_Geographic_Coverage.label: Demographic and Geographic Coverage
f15_Demographic_and_Geographic_Coverage.guidance: Who and where the data represents, and who and where it does not. A dataset that represents a population accurately says so; the field matters because its absence is what allows a model to be applied to a population nobody measured.

f16_Time_Period_Covered.label: Time Period Covered
f16_Time_Period_Covered.guidance: The span the data covers, and what happened during it. A model trained on a period of stable conditions inherits the assumption that conditions will remain stable, and the card is where that assumption is written down.

f17_Licence_and_Consent_Basis.label: Licence and Consent Basis
f17_Licence_and_Consent_Basis.guidance: The basis on which each dataset may be used, and whether consent was obtained where it was required. Where consent was not obtained, that is the fact to record, not an absence to leave blank.

f18_Preprocessing_and_Filtering.label: Preprocessing and Filtering
f18_Preprocessing_and_Filtering.guidance: What was removed, resampled or imputed, and on what basis. Filtering is where a dataset acquires the shape of the population the model will then fail on, and it is rarely the step examined.

f19_Known_Dataset_Limitations.label: Known Dataset Limitations
f19_Known_Dataset_Limitations.guidance: What the dataset cannot represent. This is the field that prevents a metric from being read as a general claim, and it is almost always empty.

f20_Evaluation_Data.label: Evaluation Data
f20_Evaluation_Data.guidance: The data the evaluation was run on, and whether it is disjoint from the training data. Disjointness is the first thing to check in any evaluation, and its absence invalidates every number in the section.

f21_Metrics.label: Metrics
f21_Metrics.guidance: Each metric, its value, and the confidence interval or sample size behind it. A single figure with no interval is a point presented as a range, and decisions get made on it.

f22_Performance_by_Subgroup.label: Performance by Subgroup
f22_Performance_by_Subgroup.guidance: The same metrics for each group the model affects, with the sample size for each. A subgroup figure from a small sample is not a measurement, and the sample size is what distinguishes the two.

f23_Baseline_Comparison.label: Baseline Comparison
f23_Baseline_Comparison.guidance: What the model is compared against, and by how much. A model compared only with a trivial baseline can be both better than it and useless.

f24_Threshold_and_Operating_Point.label: Threshold and Operating Point
f24_Threshold_and_Operating_Point.guidance: The threshold in force, and what the alternatives would cost. A model is a set of trade-offs rather than a single system, and the trade-off is only visible once a threshold is fixed.

f25_Evaluation_Method_and_Limitations.label: Evaluation Method and Limitations
f25_Evaluation_Method_and_Limitations.guidance: How the evaluation was conducted, by whom, and what it does not establish. An evaluation conducted by the team that built the model is legitimate, and it is a fact that belongs on the card.

f26_Robustness_and_Failure_Modes.label: Robustness and Failure Modes
f26_Robustness_and_Failure_Modes.guidance: How the model behaves under input it was not tested on, and the known ways it fails. Known failure modes are more useful than a robustness score, because a reader can act on them and cannot act on a score.

f27_Affected_Groups.label: Affected Groups
f27_Affected_Groups.guidance: The groups whose outcomes the model determines, named. Groups described in aggregate on the basis of a test are not the same as the group that performs worst on it.

f28_Known_Bias.label: Known Bias
f28_Known_Bias.guidance: The specific ways this model is unfair to this group, stated so that they could be false. A field titled "bias" that says the model may be biased is a heading; "the model scores this group lower on historic completion rates" is a claim that can be measured and can turn out to be wrong.

f29_Safety_Risks.label: Safety Risks
f29_Safety_Risks.guidance: The ways the model could cause harm, by severity, with the conditions under which each arises. Severity is what determines the control, and a risk listed without severity is a list of possibilities.

f30_Dual_Use_and_Misuse_Potential.label: Dual-Use and Misuse Potential
f30_Dual_Use_and_Misuse_Potential.guidance: How the model could be used to cause harm, and what has been done about it. Relevant to a model that generates as well as one that classifies, and usually unstated.

f31_Environmental_and_Resource_Impact.label: Environmental and Resource Impact
f31_Environmental_and_Resource_Impact.guidance: The energy and compute consumed, and by whom bears it. Recorded because it is a real cost that appears in no other section, and because it is usually the only figure an external party can verify.

f32_Data_Privacy_Impact.label: Data Privacy Impact
f32_Data_Privacy_Impact.guidance: What the model can reveal about individuals in its training data, and whether it has been tested for it. Extraction and memorisation are testable, and the test is the only thing that distinguishes a considered answer from an assumption.

f33_Known_Limitations.label: Known Limitations
f33_Known_Limitations.guidance: What the model cannot do, stated plainly. This is the section a reader consults after an incident, and a card that is optimistic in it is a card that will not be consulted a second time.

f34_Out_of_Distribution_Behaviour.label: Out-of-Distribution Behaviour
f34_Out_of_Distribution_Behaviour.guidance: How the model behaves on inputs unlike its training data, and whether that has been measured. A model given a population it never saw does not fail loudly, which is what makes this worth recording.

f35_Production_Monitoring.label: Production Monitoring
f35_Production_Monitoring.guidance: What is watched after deployment, against what baseline, and how often. Drift is a property of the relationship between the model and the world, not of the model, so a launch measurement is the first of a series.

f36_Monitoring_Thresholds.label: Monitoring Thresholds
f36_Monitoring_Thresholds.guidance: What result triggers action, written before the result is known. A threshold set after seeing a number is a description of that number.

f37_Retraining_and_Update_Policy.label: Retraining and Update Policy
f37_Retraining_and_Update_Policy.guidance: When the model will be retrained, what triggers it, and who approves. Without this the model is updated whenever someone has time, and the change is then invisible to everything above it in this card.

f38_Version_Change_Record.label: Version Change Record
f38_Version_Change_Record.guidance: What changed between this version and the last, and why. Models change often and silently, and a card with no change record cannot answer what was in force when an incident occurred.

f39_Decommissioning_Plan.label: Decommissioning Plan
f39_Decommissioning_Plan.guidance: How and when the model will be retired, and what happens to the data it holds. A model in production with no retirement plan is a system whose cost grows and whose obligations are never discharged.
